archetypes.name: contract-ledger
archetypes.rationale: Checks whether removing implement workflow classification preserves every documented shell/run-log/report contract while leaving design contracts intact.
archetypes.prompt_body: Investigate the plan for contract drift across run-flags, timing ledgers, summaries, report-tokens, and docs. Compare each proposed deletion or conditional rendering change against the listed scope files and identify any producer/consumer pair that the plan may leave mismatched. Pay special attention to design-vs-implement shared helpers where value-presence conditionals could accidentally change design behavior. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: schema-compat
archetypes.rationale: Targets report and JSON schema mismatches caused by dropping workflow for implement while retaining design workflow fields.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review whether the plan’s report-tokens and timing-report changes keep stable schemas where promised and intentionally omit workflow only where safe. Check for stale assumptions around RunRecord.workflow, JSON appendices, aggregate keys, per-phase grouping, and historical timing-report artifacts. Flag any place where the plan says a field remains stable but another proposed change implies removal or incompatible values. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: migration-orphans
archetypes.rationale: Looks for orphaned commands, stale fallback paths, and upgrade-state gaps after deleting implement workflow plumbing.
archetypes.prompt_body: Trace the proposed removal of --workflow, WORKFLOW_PATH, workflow-path ledger rows, and POST_PLAN_WORKFLOW_PATH through old tmpdirs, historical logs, fallback readers, tests, and docs. Look for remaining callers, dead helpers that should also be removed, or helpers the plan incorrectly removes despite design still needing them. Verify that the claimed orphan cleanup aligns with the reviewer file list and does not depend on unlisted files without justification. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
